title: CLIA Workload Tracking & Compliance Calculator
problem: Cytotechnologists must track daily slide counts to comply with CLIA's 100-slide per 24-hour limit (42 CFR 493.1274). Manual tracking across gynecological, non-gynecological, and FNA cases is error-prone. Exceeding the limit risks CLIA sanctions, fines, and potential lab certificate revocation.

skill_spec.name: CLIA Slide Workload Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Tracks daily slide screening counts against CLIA workload limits and calculates remaining capacity

outputs.name: remaining_capacity
outputs.label: Remaining slides allowed under CLIA limit

skill_spec.formula_hint: Total = gyn + non_gyn + fna + qc. CLIA max = 100/24h. Warning at 80. FNA cases may count as multiple slides depending on prep type. Calculate hourly rate = total / shift_hours.

example_queries: I've screened 45 Paps, 12 non-gyn, and 3 FNA cases so far today - how many more slides can I do?
Calculate my CLIA workload compliance for 78 gyn slides and 15 non-gyn in an 8-hour shift

title: Proficiency Testing Schedule & Deadline Tracker
problem: Cytotechnologists must pass proficiency testing events on strict schedules to maintain CLIA compliance and CAP accreditation. Missing PT deadlines or failing to document results can trigger lab sanctions. Tracking multiple PT cycles, CE deadlines, and ASCP renewal dates across different systems is burdensome.
who: All certified cytotechnologists and lab supervisors

skill_spec.name: Cytology Compliance Calendar
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of proficiency testing deadlines, ASCP renewal dates, CLIA inspection cycles, and CE requirements
skill_spec.data_domain: CLIA proficiency testing schedules, ASCP certification renewal cycles, CAP accreditation timelines for cytology labs

example_queries: When is the next proficiency testing deadline for our cytology lab?
What are the ASCP CT certification renewal requirements and CE hours needed?
What's the CMS deadline for separate CLIA certificates for remote digital slide review?

title: Bethesda System Classification Advisor
problem: Cytotechnologists encounter borderline cellular abnormalities that are difficult to classify under the Bethesda System. Distinguishing ASCUS from LSIL or LSIL from HSIL requires nuanced criteria. Misclassification can lead to missed cancer diagnoses or unnecessary patient interventions, with medicolegal consequences.
who: Junior and mid-level cytotechnologists screening Pap smears

skill_spec.name: Bethesda Classification Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Guides cytotechnologists through Bethesda System criteria for borderline cervical cytology findings
skill_spec.expertise_area: Bethesda System classification criteria for cervical cytology

example_queries: I see cells with slightly enlarged nuclei and mild hyperchromasia but no koilocytosis - ASCUS or LSIL?
What are the key Bethesda criteria to distinguish HSIL from LSIL on a ThinPrep slide?

title: QC 10% Re-screen Documentation Generator
problem: CLIA requires mandatory 10% random re-screening of negative Pap smears as quality control. Cytotechnologists must document which cases were selected, re-screening results, discrepancies found, and corrective actions. Creating these QC logs manually is tedious and error-prone, but incomplete documentation fails CAP inspections.
who: Lead and supervisory cytotechnologists responsible for QC programs

skill_spec.name: QC Re-screen Log Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates standardized CLIA-compliant 10% re-screen quality control documentation
skill_spec.structure_hint: Header (lab info, period) -> Selection method -> Cases reviewed table -> Discrepancy details -> Concordance rate calculation -> Corrective actions -> Reviewer signature -> Supervisor sign-off

example_queries: Generate a QC re-screen log for 500 negative Paps reviewed this month with 2 discrepancies
Create a 10% random re-screen documentation template for our CAP inspection

title: CAP Accreditation Inspection Checklist
problem: Preparing for CAP laboratory accreditation inspections requires verifying compliance across dozens of cytology-specific checklist items covering personnel qualifications, QC procedures, workload records, PT documentation, and SOPs. Labs often scramble before inspections, discovering gaps too late. Failed inspections can result in loss of accreditation and inability to bill Medicare.
who: Cytology lab managers and supervisory cytotechnologists

skill_spec.name: CAP Cytology Inspection Prep Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step preparation checklist for CAP cytology laboratory accreditation inspection
steps: Step 1: Verify all cytotechnologist CT(ASCP) certifications are current
Step 2: Confirm CLIA certificate is valid and posted
Step 3: Review workload records - ensure no staff exceeded 100 slides/24h
Step 4: Audit 10% QC re-screen logs for completeness
Step 5: Verify proficiency testing records for all screening personnel
Step 6: Check that SOPs are current, signed, and accessible
Step 7: Confirm specimen tracking and labeling compliance
Step 8: Review turnaround time metrics against benchmarks
Step 9: Verify equipment maintenance and calibration logs
Step 10: Audit continuing education records for all staff
Step 11: Review correlation studies (cyto-histo correlation)
Step 12: Confirm competency assessment documentation for each staff member
warnings: Warning: Missing PT records for even one technologist can trigger citation
Warning: Workload limit violations are the most common cytology-specific deficiency
Warning: New CMS guidance on remote review - verify CLIA certificate status by March 2026

example_queries: Our CAP inspection is in 3 months - give me a complete preparation checklist for our cytology lab
What are the most common cytology-specific CAP deficiencies we need to check?

title: ASCP Continuing Education Hours Calculator
problem: CT(ASCP) certification requires continuing education credits every 3 years for renewal. Cytotechnologists must track CE hours across multiple categories (cytology-specific, general lab, safety) from various providers. Miscounting hours or missing category requirements leads to certification lapse, which means inability to practice.

skill_spec.name: ASCP CE Hours Tracker & Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates continuing education hours progress toward ASCP CT certification renewal requirements

outputs.name: monthly_pace_needed
outputs.label: CE hours per month needed to meet deadline

skill_spec.formula_hint: Total required varies by ASCP pathway. Standard CT requires specific cyto hours + general. Calculate remaining = required - completed per category. Pace = remaining / months_left.

example_queries: I have 12 cytology CE hours and 8 general hours - my renewal is in 14 months, am I on track?
Calculate how many more continuing education hours I need for my ASCP CT renewal in September 2027

title: Specimen Adequacy Assessment Guide
problem: Determining whether a cytology specimen is adequate for evaluation is a critical first step that impacts all downstream diagnosis. Inadequate specimens must be correctly identified and reported per Bethesda criteria, but borderline adequacy calls are subjective. Incorrectly calling a specimen satisfactory when it's not can lead to missed pathology; calling it unsatisfactory creates unnecessary repeat procedures.

skill_spec.name: Specimen Adequacy Quick Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of Bethesda System specimen adequacy criteria for gynecological and non-gynecological cytology
skill_spec.data_domain: Bethesda System adequacy criteria, minimum cellularity requirements, obscuring factors assessment

data_hints.source_law: The Bethesda System for Reporting Cervical Cytology (3rd edition)

example_queries: What's the minimum squamous cellularity for a satisfactory ThinPrep Pap?
Slide has 60% obscuring blood - is this satisfactory or unsatisfactory per Bethesda?

title: FNA Rapid On-Site Evaluation Checklist
problem: Fine needle aspiration rapid on-site evaluation (ROSE) requires cytotechnologists to quickly assess specimen adequacy during procedures. The process is high-pressure with the patient on the table and clinician waiting. Missing steps or failing to communicate adequacy properly leads to repeat passes, patient discomfort, and wasted procedure time.

skill_spec.name: FNA ROSE Procedure Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step checklist for rapid on-site evaluation of fine needle aspiration specimens
steps: Step 1: Confirm patient identification and specimen site/laterality
Step 2: Prepare slides - air-dry for Diff-Quik, fix in alcohol for Pap stain
Step 3: Stain Diff-Quik slide (fixative 10 sec, stain I 10 sec, stain II 10 sec, rinse)
Step 4: Assess cellularity - is target tissue represented?
Step 5: Evaluate for diagnostic material vs. blood/necrosis only
Step 6: Communicate preliminary adequacy to proceduralist
Step 7: If inadequate, recommend additional pass with technique adjustment
Step 8: Triage remaining material for cell block, flow cytometry, or molecular testing
Step 9: Label all slides with patient ID, site, pass number
Step 10: Document number of passes, adequacy assessment, and triage decisions
warnings: Warning: Never give a definitive diagnosis at ROSE - adequacy assessment only
Warning: Ensure two patient identifiers on all specimens per CAP requirements
Warning: Save material for cell block before making additional smears

example_queries: Walk me through the ROSE procedure checklist for a thyroid FNA
What's the step-by-step for rapid on-site evaluation of an FNA specimen?

title: Cyto-Histo Correlation Report Generator
problem: Labs must perform cytology-histology correlation studies comparing cytology diagnoses to subsequent biopsy results. This is required for QC and CAP accreditation. Compiling correlation data, calculating discrepancy rates, and generating reports is manual and time-consuming but critical for identifying diagnostic accuracy issues.
who: Lead cytotechnologists and cytology lab managers

skill_spec.name: Cyto-Histo Correlation Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates cytology-histology correlation rates, false negative rates, and discrepancy statistics for QC reporting
skill_spec.formula_hint: Concordance = concordant / total * 100. FN rate = false_neg / (true_pos + false_neg) * 100. Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN). Industry FN rate benchmark: < 5%. Major discrepancy benchmark: < 2%.

example_queries: We had 200 cyto-histo correlations this quarter: 185 concordant, 10 minor discrepancies, 5 major - calculate our rates
What's our false negative rate if we had 3 false negatives out of 150 positive histology cases?

title: CMS Remote Review CLIA Compliance Advisor
problem: New CMS guidance (September 2025) discontinues enforcement discretion for remote digital slide review, requiring labs to obtain separate CLIA certificates by March 2026. Many cytotechnologists and labs doing telepathology are confused about requirements. Non-compliance means inability to perform remote screening, disrupting workflows and staffing models.
who: Cytotechnologists and lab directors using telepathology/remote review

skill_spec.name: CMS Remote Review Compliance Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Guides labs through CMS remote digital slide review CLIA requirements and March 2026 compliance deadline
skill_spec.expertise_area: CMS CLIA requirements for remote/digital cytology slide review and telepathology

example_queries: Our cytotechs review digital slides from home - what do we need for the March 2026 CMS deadline?
Do we need a separate CLIA certificate for each remote screening location?

title: Turnaround Time Calculator & SLA Monitor
problem: Cytology labs must meet turnaround time (TAT) benchmarks for Pap smears (typically 1-2 weeks) and urgent specimens. Calculating average TAT, identifying bottlenecks, and reporting TAT metrics for accreditation is a recurring task. Labs exceeding TAT thresholds risk patient care delays and accreditation deficiencies.

skill_spec.name: Cytology TAT Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates turnaround time statistics and identifies cases exceeding target SLAs for cytology specimens

inputs.name: sum_tat_days
inputs.label: Sum of all case TAT values (days)

skill_spec.formula_hint: Avg TAT = sum_tat / total. Compliance = within_target / total * 100. CAP benchmark: 90% of routine Paps within 10 business days. STAT within 24h.

example_queries: We processed 800 Paps this month with average TAT of 7.2 days, 92% within 10 days - how do we compare to benchmarks?
Calculate our turnaround time compliance if 45 out of 50 STAT cases were reported within 24 hours

title: Ergonomic Injury Prevention Checklist
problem: Microscopy work causes significant musculoskeletal disorders and eye strain. Cytotechnologists spend 6-8 hours daily at the microscope, leading to neck, back, shoulder, and wrist problems. Proper ergonomic setup and break schedules are critical but often neglected under workload pressure. Work-related injuries lead to lost productivity and workers' compensation claims.
who: All cytotechnologists performing daily microscopy work

skill_spec.name: Microscopy Ergonomic Safety Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Daily ergonomic setup verification and break schedule for cytotechnologists to prevent repetitive strain injuries
steps: Step 1: Adjust chair height - feet flat on floor, thighs parallel to ground
Step 2: Set microscope eyepiece height - no neck flexion beyond 15 degrees
Step 3: Position arm rests to support forearms during slide manipulation
Step 4: Verify monitor height for LIS/digital system at eye level
Step 5: Apply 20-20-20 rule - every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Step 6: Take micro-break every 30 minutes (30-second stretch)
Step 7: Take full break every 2 hours (5-10 minute walk/stretch)
Step 8: Perform neck rolls, shoulder shrugs, and wrist circles during breaks
Step 9: Check lighting - reduce glare on microscope and screens
Step 10: End of day - log any discomfort or symptoms for tracking
warnings: Warning: Report persistent numbness, tingling, or pain to occupational health immediately
Warning: OSHA requires employers to address known ergonomic hazards under General Duty Clause

example_queries: Give me a daily ergonomic checklist for my microscopy workstation
What's the recommended break schedule for cytotechnologists to prevent repetitive strain?

They need guidance on transitioning to molecular cytology, digital pathology, FNA specialization, or management roles to remain relevant in an evolving field.

skill_spec.expertise_area: Cytotechnology career development, molecular diagnostics transition, digital pathology skills, advanced certification paths

Is the Master's degree requirement worth it if I'm 8 years from retirement?
